correctness.rationale: PASS: The local variation equals |y_i-y_{i-1}|+2dist(m_i,[ell_i,u_i]); compact convex LP duality gives max_{p_i in [-1,1]} sum_i[p_i a_i-u_i p_i^+ +ell_i p_i^-]-lambda d sum_i|p_{i+1}-p_i|. For each real p coordinate, ternary threshold layers over h in (0,1) satisfy exact coarea |p_i-p_{i+1}|=int |s_i(h)-s_{i+1}(h)|dh, so max attained on ternary labels and solved by 3 fixed starting labels with 3-state cyclic DP in O(n). The constant labels force total average A in [L,U] for zero extra variation. For nonconstant ternary labels, splitting positive and negative indicator runs into proper cyclic intervals gives exactly two cut edges per interval; maximizing interval deficits yields d_*=max(0,max_I sum_I(ell_i-a_i),max_I sum_I(a_i-u_i))/(2lambda). The arbitrary-budget formula follows by taking maximum of (R_s-t)_+/(lambda C_s) among labels with nonzero boundary; unbounded fluxes realize all corrected mean vectors with total A, giving dist(A,[L,U]). A new independent checker compared the ternary dual with a primal LP in 110 deterministic bounded cases n=2..6. These numerical checks support, not prove, the universal coarea/minimax theorem.
